solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Crime rings left in charge, getting intoxicants here

indicators.note: to ring something is to encircle it, so the first word's letters go round the next ones

parts.note: i/c is the usual abbreviation for in charge

explanation.surface: A criminal ring stays in control while its members get high.
explanation.walkthrough: An off-licence is a British shop licensed to sell alcohol for drinking elsewhere; i/c is the standard shorthand for in charge.
explanation.definitionFit: An off-licence is a liquor store, the place where you buy alcoholic drinks to take away.

clue.text: I will catch cold — not again!

indicators.note: catching something means holding it inside, so one piece goes into the other

parts.note: the Roman numeral I is one
C for cold, as on a tap

explanation.surface: Someone who has caught a chill vows never to repeat the experience.
explanation.definitionFit: Something done once happens a single time and is not repeated.

clue.text: Reason to get a 14 in a packet

definitions.meaning: you would get a squeezebox (14-down) for a tune
second meaning: a large sum of money

explanation.surface: Someone wonders why an accordion would arrive in a parcel.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is whimsical: an accordion is wanted FOR (the sake of a) TUNE. 'A packet' is British slang for lots of money.
explanation.definitionFit: A packet and a fortune are both informal ways of saying a very large amount of money.

clue.text: Benefit is mentioned, tucking into cool drink

indicators.note: tucking into something means going inside it, so the phrase sits within the other words

parts.note: a topic that comes up is mentioned

explanation.surface: A fact is raised while someone gulps down a cold drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tucking into' sounds like eating, but it puts the mentioning phrase inside the cool drink. Income Support was a British means-tested welfare payment.
explanation.definitionFit: Income Support is a UK state welfare payment, so it is a kind of social security benefit.

clue.text: Squire's back with page, really

indicators.note: the back of a word is its rear end, so only its final letter is kept

parts.note: a verso is a left-hand page of a book

explanation.surface: The squire's rear view of a pageboy is described with emphasis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Back' and 'page' together suggest verso, the back of a leaf, but 'back' selects from squire and 'page' alone gives VERSO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ever so is an informal intensifier meaning very or truly, so it can stand for really.

clue.text: Top British wartime commander

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a knitted woollen jacket worn on the upper body
second meaning: Lord ..., who led the Charge of the Light Brigade in the Crimean War

explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' looks like an adjective praising the commander; it is a garment. The cardigan was named after the Earl himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A cardigan is a buttoned knitted garment for the upper body, and the 7th Earl of Cardigan was a cavalry general.

clue.text: Tip of finger on buzzer in Hereford, say

indicators.note: one piece sits on, or after, the other in this across answer
the tip of something is its very end, here its leading letter

explanation.surface: A fingertip presses a buzzer in the English city of Hereford.
explanation.walkthrough: Hereford is not the city but a breed of cattle raised for meat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hereford cattle are a breed reared for meat, so a Hereford is an example of beef stock.

clue.text: Parisian in grand lady's housing when queens have gone off, maybe?

definitions.text: when queens have gone off, maybe?

indicators.note: housing something means giving it a home inside, so the lady's word encloses another

parts.note: a dame is a grand lady
G is slang for a grand, a thousand

explanation.surface: A French woman lives with an elderly noblewoman whose queens have died.
explanation.walkthrough: DAME houses G just after its first letter. The queens are chess pieces exchanged off the board.
explanation.definitionFit: In chess the endgame is the final phase, often reached once both sides' queens have been traded.

clue.text: After organising fair, Ed runs charity event

indicators.note: organising means arranging things into a new order, so these letters get rearranged

explanation.surface: Having run a village fair, Ed goes on to organise a charity do.
explanation.definitionFit: A fundraiser is an event held to collect money for a cause, typically a charity.

clue.text: Wow — whizz around lake in this?

definitions.text: Wow — whizz around lake in this?

parts.note: cor is a British exclamation of surprise

indicators.note: around means encircling, so one word's letters go about another

parts.note: a whizz is an expert, an ace

explanation.surface: An exclaimed suggestion to zip round a lake in some small craft.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is also the definition: a coracle is a small round boat in which you might paddle round a lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A coracle is a small round Welsh boat of wicker and hide, used on lakes and rivers.

clue.text: Fast or fleet run towards the west, then north

indicators.note: in an across answer west is the left, so the letter is lifted out and moved to the front
then means next in sequence, so the last piece follows

parts.note: R for run, as in cricket scoring
an armada is a fleet of warships

explanation.surface: A fleet, or a quick one, sails west and then north.
explanation.walkthrough: The R in ARMADA moves one place west to the front, giving RAMADA, then N follows. 'Fast' looks like 'quick'; it is the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Ramadan is the Islamic month of daytime fasting, so it is a fast in the religious sense.

clue.text: Staffs cricketers stop a drive? That's novel

parts.note: to staff a post is to man it
the field is the fielding side in cricket
you park when you stop driving

explanation.surface: Staffordshire's fielders stop a batsman's drive, which is something new.
explanation.walkthrough: Staffs looks like the abbreviation for Staffordshire, an English county, but it is the verb. A drive is also a cricket shot.
explanation.definitionFit: Mansfield Park is a novel by Jane Austen, published in 1814.

clue.text: Entry of player put on the bench, culminating in goal

indicators.note: culminating means ending with, so the second piece comes last

parts.note: a substitute sits on the bench
a mission is a goal or aim

explanation.surface: A footballer on the bench comes on and ends up scoring.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Goal' suggests football scoring; it means an aim.
explanation.definitionFit: A submission is an entry sent in, as to a competition or for judging.

clue.text: Coastal town's atmosphere picked up

indicators.note: picked up means heard, so the word goes by its sound

explanation.surface: Someone senses the sea air of a seaside resort.
explanation.definitionFit: Ayr is a town on the west coast of Scotland, on the Firth of Clyde.

clue.text: Fight started by lover, one held tightly by musician

indicators.note: something started by another has the other at its head, so that piece goes first

parts.note: a squeeze is a boyfriend or girlfriend

explanation.surface: A lovers' quarrel ends with a musician held in a tight embrace.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is cryptic: an accordion is squeezed in the player's arms.
explanation.definitionFit: A squeezebox is an accordion or concertina, an instrument the musician squeezes against the chest.

clue.text: Feeling ill as taking drug, Sally drops everything

indicators.note: taking something in means holding it inside
dropping means letting go, so a word for everything is removed

parts.note: qua means in the capacity of, as

explanation.surface: Sally has been on drugs and feels sick, so she gives up all her habits.
explanation.walkthrough: QUA is Latin-derived 'as'; SALLY loses ALL, a synonym of everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Queasy describes nausea, the sick sensation of being about to vomit.

clue.text: Asian dish — Jo and Alfred won't finish unknown one

indicators.note: not finishing means stopping short, so each name loses its final letter

parts.note: algebra uses x, y and z for unknowns

explanation.surface: Two diners leave a strange curry unfinished.
explanation.definitionFit: A jalfrezi is a spicy curry with peppers and onions from South Asian cooking.

clue.text: Maker of Rolls, say, with large wheels and brown line in London

parts.note: L for large, as on clothing
two O shapes look like a pair of wheels

explanation.surface: A maker of Rolls-Royce cars, with big wheels, is on a London route.
explanation.walkthrough: Rolls suggests the car maker; it is bread rolls.
explanation.definitionFit: The Bakerloo line is a London Underground route shown in brown on the Tube map.

clue.text: Erstwhile knight not primarily a paragon

indicators.note: primarily points at the first letter, and not means it is dropped

parts.note: a Knight Templar was a medieval crusading knight

explanation.surface: A former knight is no longer quite the model of virtue.
explanation.definitionFit: An exemplar is a perfect model to be copied, as a paragon is.

clue.text: Monument with scrubbed exterior borders parking for shops

indicators.note: to border something is to surround it on each side
scrubbing off the exterior strips the outer letters away

explanation.surface: A monument is cleaned and hemmed in by a car park near the shops.
explanation.definitionFit: Emporia is a plural of emporium, a large store, so it means shops.

clue.text: Tom, perhaps, meeting English underworld figure

parts.note: a tom is a male cat, a he-cat

explanation.surface: A man named Tom meets an English gangster.
explanation.walkthrough: Tom looks like a man's name; it is a tomcat.
explanation.definitionFit: Hecate is the Greek goddess of witchcraft linked with the realm of the dead.

clue.text: Said a substance like sodium nitrate is in battery

indicators.note: said means spoken, so the phrase is judged on its sound

explanation.surface: A chemical such as sodium nitrate is found inside a battery cell.
explanation.walkthrough: Battery suggests electric cells; it is the legal sense of physical attack.
explanation.definitionFit: Assault and battery are paired legal terms, and battery is a physical attack on a person.

clue.text: Unlike Victoria, Bill welcomes inspiration

indicators.note: welcoming someone means taking them in, so one word goes inside the other

parts.note: an ad, or advertisement, is a bill
a muse is a source of inspiration

explanation.surface: Bill, unlike the old Queen, opens his door to a spark of genius.
explanation.walkthrough: Queen Victoria is famously quoted as saying 'We are not amused'.
explanation.definitionFit: Victoria was reputedly not amused, so one who is amused is unlike her.

clue.text: Go quickly, possibly fly

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to move at speed
second meaning: a fastener, as on the fly of trousers

explanation.walkthrough: 'Fly' reads as a verb continuing 'go quickly'; it is the trouser opening.
explanation.definitionFit: To zip is to speed along, and a zip is the fastener often used on a trouser fly.

clue.text: Plain clothing fashions not showy enough

indicators.note: clothing something covers it, so the first word wraps the second

explanation.surface: Plain clothes are judged too drab to be fashionable.
explanation.definitionFit: Being overmodest means being too humble, failing to show off as much as one could.

clue.text: Don Quixote finally gets involved in combat

indicators.note: getting involved in something means entering it
finally points at the end, keeping just the last letter

explanation.surface: Don Quixote at last joins battle, as he tilted at windmills.
explanation.walkthrough: Don looks like the Spanish title; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To don clothes is to put them on, to wear them.

clue.text: Stole large bags robbers emptied, getting time in correctional facility

indicators.note: to bag something is to put it inside

parts.note: a boa is a long scarf, a stole

indicators.note: emptied means its insides are cleared out, leaving only the outer letters

parts.note: the first and last letters of robbers

explanation.surface: Robbers took a stash of loot and got time in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: BOA with L bags RS plus T. 'Stole' looks like the verb of theft; it is a scarf. A borstal was a British detention centre for young offenders.
explanation.definitionFit: A borstal was a British institution for reforming young offenders, a correctional facility for youths.

clue.text: Act, say, securing leads in university theatre

indicators.note: securing something means holding it fast inside
leads are the front-runners, so the first letters of the next words are taken

parts.note: the first letters of university and theatre

explanation.surface: An actor speaks a line holding a prominent role in a campus theatre.
explanation.walkthrough: Act looks theatrical with theatre nearby; it means a law.
explanation.definitionFit: A statute is a law passed by a legislature, an Act of Parliament.

clue.text: Cross parents when children get excited

explanation.surface: Annoyed parents at a time when their children are worked up.
explanation.walkthrough: Cross reads as angry; it is the letter X.
explanation.definitionFit: Xmas is Christmas, the festive time youngsters most look forward to.

clue.text: Ran desktop after treatment for bug

indicators.note: treatment works something over, so the letters come out in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A desktop computer was run after being cleaned of a software glitch.
explanation.walkthrough: Bug suggests a computer fault; it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A pond skater is a water insect that glides on the surface film, and true bugs include it.
